extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers and journal editors in general medical journals
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and guiding the quality of peer reviews for general medical journals using the 7‑item Review Quality Instrument (RQI) and associated operational norms. Includes scoring guidance, empirically identified predictors of high-quality reviews, and practical reviewer recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: The importance of the research question
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the reviewer addressed the importance of the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of seven RQI items; scored 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Reviewers should evaluate whether the study asks a question of clinical or scientific significance and explain why the question matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of the question
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer's discussion of the originality of the question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and comment on novelty compared with existing literature. Place the work in context and justify claims of originality or lack thereof. Scored 1–5 on the RQI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and weaknesses of the method
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer's assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss study design, sampling, measurement, analysis, biases, confounding, and other methodological aspects. If the reviewer lacks statistical/epidemiological training they should request a statistical co-reviewer rather than skip assessment of methods. Scored 1–5 on the RQI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of the paper (writing, organisation, illustrations, tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer's assessment of the presentation of the paper (writing, organisation, illustrations, tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on clarity of writing, logical organisation, adequacy and clarity of tables/figures, and whether presentation aids understanding. Provide specific examples of unclear passages or problematic figures. Scored 1–5 on the RQI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of the results
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer's assessment of the interpretation of the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the authors' conclusions are supported by the data, consider issues of causation vs association, overinterpretation, and alternative explanations. Offer suggestions for tempering or strengthening interpretation. Scored 1–5 on the RQI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provided constructive comments and substantiated the comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which the reviewer provided constructive comments and substantiated the comments (with reasoning, evidence, examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should be accompanied by explanation, evidence or examples and, where possible, concrete suggestions for improvement. Assertions without substantiation are insufficient. This is RQI item 6 and is scored 1–5; operational norm: substantiate every criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global overall quality of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Global overall quality of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An overall judgement of the review's usefulness, thoroughness, fairness, and clarity. This is the seventh RQI item and is scored 1–5, summarising the reviewer's performance across other items.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7‑item Review Quality Scoring Form (scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the seven dimensions of the RQI is scored 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RQI provides a simple numeric scale for each domain; editors and researchers use aggregated scores to assess review quality. Use the scale consistently and justify high/low scores with examples from the review text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirically identified predictors of high-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Predictors that were statistically associated with higher-quality reviews in multivariate analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key predictors: training in epidemiology or statistics (the only factor significant for both editors' and authors' assessments); younger age (up to ~60 years) significant for editors' assessments; North American residence (possibly reflecting language/writing style) significant for both editors and authors; and not being on the journal's editorial board (significant for authors' assessments). These are correlates, not prescriptive requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process‑quality norms for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Norms about how reviewer behaviour and timing relate to review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review quality increases with time spent up to ~3 hours and then plateaus; reviewers spending less than one hour produce systematically lower-quality reviews. Turnaround time is independent of quality (fast reviews can be good). Author/institution characteristics explain only ~8% of variance: most quality depends on reviewer behaviour during the review itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational norms and actionable reviewer guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical recommendations derived from the study for producing higher-quality reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should address every RQI item in their report; schedule at least 2–3 hours for a substantial empirical paper; reviewers without statistical training should ask the editor for a statistical co-reviewer rather than skip methodological assessment; and reviewers should substantiate every criticism (provide reasoning, evidence, examples). These are operational best practices to improve review quality.
